searchText: Hi all consensus devs, we’ve made some changes to the blob schedule PR. What do we think of this now? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4277 i see some misses with lighthouse nethermind pairs in http://138.199.172.61:8082/, <@466006586477772831> can you check? participation dropped from 91 -> 85 something happened between slot 67320 to 67485 thanks, can I have access to the logs please<@288990561279541248> <@466006586477772831> I believe the root cause is the storage space (file system), 157 GB per host while previously processing more than 30 blobs per block, that's why it reach the limits before retention period http://94.130.19.237:3000/d/rYdddlPWk/node-exporter-full?orgId=1&from=now-24h&to=now&timezone=browser&var-datasource=default&var-job=node&var-node=peerdas-devnet-ssl-15-lighthouse-geth-1&var-diskdevices=%5Ba-z%5D%2B%7Cnvme%5B0-9%5D%2Bn%5B0-9%5D%2B%7Cmmcblk%5B0-9%5D%2B&refresh=1m thanks i was investigating all this while, trying to find something in nethermind, but thankfully haven't I think you should have access: https://github.com/testinprod-io/ethereum-devnets/blob/main/ansible/inventories/peerdas-devnet-ssl-15/group_vars/lighthouse.yaml. However, I've also sent you the logs via DM if you want to have a look some prysm nethermind pairs went into syncing, can you check <@531934490826768418> / <@363800010518822915> ? `prysm-nethermind-5,7,9` I can see that these nodes have consumed most of storage too. It seems like some nodes have used most while others haven't. oh alright atleast it's not a protocol issue Hmm but most of prysm and lighthouse supernodes seem to be out of storage. Grandine supernodes have 80+% as well. I'm bit concerned that we might see more nodes going into syncing which means we have bug in our persisting columns, a few columns might have missed i don't think so, you might as well group columns by block root and store them in your database, instead of a block_root -> sidecar mapping in that case you may need lesser storage nimbus might be at around 70 gigs? can you check once? what's each hosts storage at the moment? might wanna consult <@412614104222531604> for this and wanna bump the storage up also we are nowhere close to 18-ish days, so there _might_ be other problems too Nimbus supernodes used around 90GiB atm nice We are running from DigitalOcean with 160GB for each node, but it seems like we need to increase this size that's 70 gigs of columns easily, but how many days are we into the network Might be worth observing if we can catch other issues as well just 9 days just after midnight on 22nd April UTC i don't think there would be an issue with prysm syncing as most of the network has run fairly stable so far, can you try bumping the storage of those specific hosts, i'm not sure by how much tho pretty sure we ran into the same issue and we had to bump all nodes to 250gb supernodes just hold on to an insane amount of data with many columns after 18 days it shouldn't grow anymore tho how old is the network? 9 days something weird is happening maybe yeah not gonna make it with 160gb right how long do we keep the network? the issue is previously the network ran with 64/48 blobs per block easily 2-3 more weeks we need to run sync tests, some of us do okay, and we have 9 days more in retention period, think we can hold on with 100gb more on super node or maybe 150g `256kb * 9 blobs * 32 slots * 225 epochs * 9 days` Okay, we are internally discussing to increase to something like 320GB only for the nodes that need an upsize Please let me know if you guys are fine with this This will need a reboot of the nodes affected We’ve just doubled the storage for the nodes that were out of storage and could not sync further. Will take a closer look to them and please feel free to ask any questions Are there any client teams that are peerdas-devnet-7 ready? https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/peerdas-devnet-7 if so, we could target a launch tomorrow. For Grandine, we still need to fix sync issue, and given the situation in sunnyside devnet rn, it is a good place to hardening syncing strategy https://hackmd.io/@willcorcoran/S111Y-bgel Summary of PeerDAS-related discussions from ACDC 156 / PeerDAS Breakout Room Call 28 Preparation cc: <@539495253418180618> <@412614104222531604> let me know if you need a hand with the peerdas-devnet-7 spec HackMD. I noticed that there was a recent commit in lodestar related to this. I've updated the nodes to the latest PeerDAS branch, but the full & super nodes seem to use similar amount of bandwidth regardless of custody. Are there any other pending fixes for this, or is there anything that needs to be updated on the nodes by any chance?
